questions.question: How many distinct tokens are in VOCAB for this reward-model demo?
options: 12: six GOOD tokens plus six BAD tokens
3: one token for each prompt
6: only the GOOD vocabulary is retained
24: every token appears once for each pair position
questions.explanation: GOOD and BAD are disjoint six-token tuples, and VOCAB is the sorted set of their concatenation, giving 12 entries.

questions.question: What kind of examples does sample_pair(rng) create for reward-model training?
options: Two prompts with identical completions
A random prompt, a two-GOOD-token response, and a two-BAD-token response
One response with one token drawn from every vocabulary entry
A terminal state and an action from GridWorld
questions.explanation: sample_pair chooses x from PROMPTS, then draws y_pos from GOOD twice and y_neg from BAD twice.

questions.question: How does train_rm update a token's weight after comparing y_pos and y_neg?
options: It copies the positive score into every token and leaves negatives unchanged
It subtracts the learning rate from every vocabulary entry
It adds lr*(1-p)*count to positive tokens and subtracts the same scale from negative tokens
It updates only the prompt embedding, never response tokens
questions.explanation: With p=sigmoid(r_pos-r_neg), grad_scale=1-p; bag counts scale positive additions and negative subtractions.

questions.question: Why does score(w, ['clear', 'clear']) count the weight for 'clear' twice?
options: score applies a softmax to duplicate words
The second token is treated as a negative label
Only the first occurrence is used by Counter
bag(tokens) records token multiplicity, and score sums w[token] * count
questions.explanation: score iterates over bag(tokens).items(), so repeated tokens contribute their weight once per occurrence.

questions.question: What reward does rlhf_loop assign to a sampled token?
options: The reward-model token score minus beta times KL(policy || reference)
Only the binary verifier result; beta is ignored
The token index plus the number of prompts
The negative of the reward-model score, with KL added
questions.explanation: The loop sets reward = rm_score - beta * kl_term, penalizing movement away from the copied reference policy.

questions.question: How are policy advantages normalized in one rlhf_loop update?
options: Each reward is divided by its token index
They are (reward - batch mean) divided by batch standard deviation plus 1e-8
All advantages are replaced by the reward-model weights
They are sorted so the best completion always has advantage one
questions.explanation: The 16 rollout rewards are centered by mean_r and scaled by sqrt(var_r)+1e-8 before the clipped policy update.
